evidence.excerpt: Oxygen transmission rate was measured on commercial and laboratory-cast LLDPE films of three densities (0.918, 0.924, 0.932 g/cm³) across a temperature range of 5 °C to 50 °C. Arrhenius plots were constructed from OTR data collected at seven temperature points; activation energies for permeation ranged from 28.4 to 41.7 kJ/mol and increased with film density, in line with reduced chain mobility at higher crystallinity. Positron annihilation lifetime spectroscopy (PALS) performed in collaboration with a partner institution provided free-volume hole radius estimates of 0.26–0.31 nm at 23 °C. A positive correlation (R² = 0.91) between hole radius and permeability coefficient was observed. Pre-exponential diffusivity factors derived from the Arrhenius fits correlated with crystallinity index from DSC. These data are intended as reference parameters for shelf-life modelling of chilled food products stored at variable temperatures.
